posts.title: Victim Carjacked At Gunpoint Wednesday
posts.description: Delaware State Police are investigating an armed robbery and carjacking that occurred Wednesday night in a restaurant parking lot in Newark. On November 25, 2026, at approximately 10:10 p.m., troopers responded to the 100 block of Geoffrey Drive following a report of an armed robbery. According to investigators, two masked suspects, one armed with a rifle, approached the victim and demanded personal belongings and the victim’s vehicle. The victim complied, and the suspects fled in the stolen vehicle and a second vehicle. The victim was not injured. The Delaware State Police Criminal Investigation Unit assumed responsibility for the investigation. On Thursday, November 26, 2026, troopers located the stolen vehicle in the 300 block of East 14th Street in Wilmington.

posts.title: Troopers ID Victim In Fox Run Killing
posts.description: On Monday, a 36-year-old Bear woman has been arrested on first-degree murder and related charges following the fatal shooting of her father at the Fox Run Shopping Center in Bear, according to Delaware State Police. Officials said on November 23, 2026, at approximately 10:12 a.m., troopers responded to the shopping center in the 100 block of Fox Hunt Drive for a reported shooting. Upon arrival, troopers located the suspect, who was still armed with a handgun, and took her into custody in the parking lot. Troopers located a 56-year-old man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds and rendered first aid until emergency medical personnel arrived. He was transported to an area hospital, where he was later pronounced dead. The Delaware State Police have since identified the victim as 56-year-old Ricardo Victoria of Kennesaw, Georgia. posts.title: Police: She Got Her Nails Did on a 99-Year-Old’s Dime: Caregiver Lands Behind Bars
posts.description: A 29-year-old caregiver is facing criminal charges following an investigation into unauthorized credit card transactions involving a 99-year-old woman, according to the New Castle County Division of Police. On September 8, 2026, officers responded to a residence and launched an investigation into fraudulent credit card activity. During the investigation, officers reviewed the victim’s credit card statements with a family member who held power of attorney and discovered numerous unauthorized transactions. Investigators also determined that the victim’s credit card was missing. The unauthorized transactions included multiple cash withdrawals at a business in Philadelphia, as well as purchases at a nail salon and restaurant in Wilmington. Police subsequently identified a 29-year-old woman assigned to provide care for the victim as the suspect and obtained a warrant for her arrest.
